column2: Acute fever, purulent sputum, pleuritic pain, high CRP and lobar consolidation is bacterial pneumonia triggering the asthma attack; give antibiotics.
Fever, pleuritic pain and rusty sputum with cold sores is pneumococcal lobar pneumonia; the fever reactivates herpes simplex.
Pneumonia within 14 days of travel to the Arabian Peninsula meets the possible MERS case definition: isolate and send MERS-CoV PCR.
Pneumonia ≥ 48 h after admission is hospital-acquired (Gram-negatives, S. aureus): treat per local HAP policy, not CAP protocol.
Late-onset HAP (≥ 5 days) is caused by resistant Gram-negatives (Pseudomonas, Klebsiella, Acinetobacter) and MRSA.
Hospital-acquired pneumonia carries ~30% mortality (older, sicker patients, resistant organisms).
Fever with multiple cavitating peripheral nodules in a drug injector is septic emboli from tricuspid endocarditis (S. aureus); blood cultures and echo.
IGRA uses TB-specific antigens absent from BCG, so it is more specific than the TST; a positive result means treat latent TB once active TB is excluded.
A cold psoas abscess with back pain and weight loss suggests spinal TB (Pott disease): send pus for AFB, culture and molecular testing.
Bilateral hilar nodes with erythema nodosum, ankle arthritis and fever is Löfgren syndrome (acute sarcoidosis), which usually remits.
Sinusitis, conductive deafness, subglottic stenosis and multiple lung nodules are GPA; check c-ANCA (PR3), urine and biopsy.
Tularaemia (Francisella) follows contact with rabbits or muskrats. Psittacosis = birds, Q fever = sheep/cattle, leptospirosis = rat urine.
Acute eosinophilic pneumonia after starting smoking (> 25% BAL eosinophils) responds dramatically to high-dose IV methylprednisolone.
Diffuse alveolar haemorrhage gives progressively bloodier BAL with haemosiderin-laden macrophages after 48–72 h.
Fibrosing mediastinitis follows burnt-out histoplasmosis or TB; drugs do not reverse it, and stenoses are stented.
S. pneumoniae is the commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia at all ages.
CURB-65: confusion, urea > 7, RR ≥ 30, low BP, age ≥ 65. A respiratory rate of 20 is not a criterion.
Mycoplasma pneumonia with erythema multiforme and cold-agglutinin haemolytic anaemia; treat with a macrolide or doxycycline.
Pneumonia with myalgia after acquiring parrots is psittacosis (Chlamydia psittaci); treat with doxycycline.
Injecting drug users get S. aureus pneumonia (haematogenous or cavitating); blood cultures, echo and MRSA cover.
Pneumonia is defined by new radiographic shadowing, so the chest X-ray confirms it; cultures identify an organism in a minority.
Alveolar macrophages ingest M. tuberculosis and, activated by T-cell IFN-γ, become epithelioid and Langhans giant cells forming granulomas.
Standard TB therapy: 2 months RIPE then 4 months RI (with pyridoxine); streptomycin is no longer first line.
Rifampicin turns urine, sweat and tears orange-red and is a potent enzyme inducer (pill, warfarin, steroids).
Nasal crusting, cavitating nodules, AKI and mononeuritis multiplex form the ENT–lung–kidney pattern of GPA; check PR3-ANCA.
Asthma with eosinophilia, IgE > 1000 kU/L and infiltrates is ABPA; oral prednisolone first line, itraconazole as steroid-sparing.
Löfgren syndrome (erythema nodosum with BHL) has the best prognosis in sarcoidosis, usually remitting within 2 years.
Aspiration during a seizure with foul sputum days later is anaerobic pneumonia; treat with anaerobic cover (co-amoxiclav).
Recent alcohol-related unconsciousness causes aspiration pneumonia in a dependent segment (right middle/lower lobe); cover anaerobes.
Necrotising pneumonia with cavities and empyema after influenza is S. aureus; add flucloxacillin (or MRSA cover).
Haemoptysis, alveolar shadowing and nephritis with negative ANCA suggest anti-GBM (Goodpasture) disease; smoking predisposes to the bleeding.
Gastric acid aspiration (Mendelson syndrome) causes chemical pneumonitis within hours with bronchospasm, tachypnoea and hypoxaemia.
Poor asthma control with brown mucus plugs and fleeting infiltrates is ABPA (IgE > 1000, Aspergillus IgE/IgG).
Bronchiectasis is a chronic structural sequela of severe pneumonia; empyema, abscess and fistula are acute complications.
Atypical pneumonia in a barracks with cold agglutinins and an X-ray worse than the signs is Mycoplasma; treat with a macrolide.
Only new confusion meets a CURB-65 criterion here (urea 5.2, RR 27, BP 100/70 and age 62 all score zero).
First-line TB drugs are hepatotoxic, so baseline LFTs are essential; also renal function, HIV/hepatitis serology and visual acuity.
ARDS is diffuse alveolar damage with protein-rich alveolar fluid and hyaline membranes, causing refractory hypoxaemia.
Type 1 failure (V/Q mismatch): asthma, emphysema, PE. Chronic bronchitis ('blue bloater') typically causes type 2 failure.
Severe hypoxaemia with bilateral crackles within a week of a viral infection and a normal echo fits ARDS (Berlin definition).
Refractory hypoxaemia with bilateral infiltrates and normal heart size in COVID-19 is ARDS; dexamethasone and critical-care support.
Remdesivir is the only listed drug with evidence in hospitalised COVID-19 on oxygen; dexamethasone 6 mg is the key treatment.
ARDS reduces (not increases) lung compliance; complications include barotrauma, VAP, multi-organ failure and fibrosis.
PaO2/FiO2 ≤ 100 mmHg on PEEP ≥ 5 with new bilateral infiltrates is severe ARDS (Berlin); prone ventilation 12–16 h/day.
With plateau 26 cmH2O there is room to raise PEEP to 12 to recruit alveoli while keeping plateau ≤ 30; tidal volume is already 6 mL/kg.
NIV fails often in severe ARDS and delays intubation; it works in hypercapnic COPD and cardiogenic pulmonary oedema.
A spontaneous breathing trial needs haemodynamic stability; ongoing vasopressor dependence is a contraindication.
Early (exudative) ARDS shows diffuse alveolar damage with protein-rich oedema and hyaline membranes.
